variant_reviews.comparison: Compute sign(sign(x) times max(|x|-lambda,0)), or equivalently return sign(x) when |x|>lambda and zero otherwise. Equality at the threshold is zero, and a zero input stays zero; retaining only sign(x) or using >= would change boundary behavior. The output is ternary {-1,0,1}, not the soft-thresholded real magnitude that appears inside the outer sign. Real.sign has sign(0)=0 and the positive-part identity supplies the scalar maximum, so their elementary case analysis gives the stated form, including Q_0=sign. Apply the same operation independently to each coordinate; this is not vector-norm thresholding, stochastic rounding or a privacy mechanism by itself.

variant_reviews.comparison: Each machine j computes its own mean with denominator n_j over H_j, applies the coordinatewise Q_lambdaN threshold and sends one ternary vector to the trusted server. Unequal machine sizes of comparable order are allowed; replacing n_j with a common N/m changes this recipe. Call the archived DPVote on the m vectors with the given selection count and privacy parameters. Its dependency first peels noisy stability maxima without replacement using epsilon/2 and delta/2, then samples selected signs with probabilities proportional to exp(epsilon-prime times the corresponding utility/4), where epsilon-prime has its separately specified factor 4 sqrt(2 s-tilde log(2/delta)). PMF.ofFintype can encode the three positive normalized sign masses but supplies neither the peeling noise nor privacy composition. Preserve the score/utility distinction, unresolved noise-independence/tie conventions, and coordinate association/zero extension needed to turn the returned support and sign set into a vector. Privacy is for replacing one entire machine dataset in the trusted-curator setting, not record-level protection or hiding the messages from that server. Population sign consistency needs the theorem's threshold/signal regime; the definition does not repair its missing upper-threshold restriction.

variant_reviews.comparison: Color each of the n vertices independently and uniformly from K+1 colors, or use the uniform law on all functions Fin n→Fin(K+1) and prove its independent coordinate law. Colorfulness on V is InjOn mu V, requiring distinct colors for every pair of distinct vertices, including nonadjacent pairs. A graph's ordinary proper coloring only separates adjacent vertices and would be insufficient. For |V|=K+1, the favorable restricted assignments are bijections to the color set, counted by (K+1)! after identifying the two finite types; the total number is (K+1)^(K+1). This yields the displayed r, with K a nonnegative integer and a nonempty color set. The stated r is not the probability for arbitrary subset cardinalities. The coloring law is auxiliary algorithmic randomness independent of the graph data, not a coloring selected adaptively after observing edge weights.

Enumerate each undirected edge once, preserve its weight, and do not insert an automorphism multiplier here—the outer approximation applies that factor separately.

variant_reviews.comparison: Set t=ceil(1/r) and generate 2t independent colorings, with one array for A and a separate array for B, independent of the observed graphs. For each unrooted tree class H with K edges, use the product of the two t-sample averages, weighted by aut(H), and sum classes once; the same coloring arrays are shared across all tree classes. This is not the average of t paired products and does not use one common coloring array across both graphs. Feed the centered adjacency matrices into X_H, then multiply the full Y_T by beta/r^2. Both factors of r are needed because each colorful count has conditional expectation r times the full weighted count. Beta contains rho^K and can be negative, distinct from the expected statistic's rho^(2K). The graph laws under the alternative can be dependent while the auxiliary coloring arrays remain independent. The theorem's probability must include this randomness, not hold for every fixed coloring. Arithmetic assembly does not establish its variance bound, detection threshold or n^(2+o(1)) computation.
